title: Force Field Balance
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI-Native Schools
description: Calculate the driving, restraining, and net forces for a school change, before and after reducing two restraining forces, then explore with sliders.

learningObjectives: The learner will calculate the total driving force, the total restraining force, and the net force for a change situation, before and after reducing two restraining forces, correctly answering three of three questions.
prerequisites: Force field analysis, driving forces, restraining forces, and the unfreeze stage, from the section "Lewin: Unfreeze, Change, Refreeze" in Chapter 17.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Commit an answer, then read the feedback and the reason
keyQuestions: Driving forces are 4, 3, 3, and 4. What is the total?
Restraining forces are 4, 3, 1, and 1. What is the net if driving is 14?
commonMisconceptions: The way to overcome resistance is to push harder
A balanced situation is stable and safe
All forces are equally easy to change
assessmentOpportunities: Driving forces are 4, 3, 3, and 4. What is the total?
Restraining forces are 4, 3, 1, and 1. What is the net if driving is 14?
Is a balanced field stable and safe?
Why reduce a restraining force rather than push harder?

controls.name: Q1, Q2, Q3 answer boxes
controls.description: Type a whole number for each question.

controls.name: Check answers
controls.description: Checks the answers; two tries per question.

controls.name: Unlock the sliders
controls.description: Shows the totals and the eight sliders after all three questions are settled.

controls.name: Reset strengths
controls.description: Returns every force to its starting strength.
